rows.reader_situation_and_job: A professional defining an AI-assisted review workflow needs to decide which judgment remains with a human reviewer before the next action.

hook_and_payoff.opening_exact: A request can look complete and still need a human decision.
hook_and_payoff.promise: Explain the difference between apparent completeness and a decision that still requires human responsibility.
hook_and_payoff.delivered_payoff: Paragraph 2 names a fictional flag-proposal step followed by reviewer checking; paragraph 4 directs the reader to identify the retained decision.

rows.central_claim: In the illustrated workflow, making the review step visible does not establish the error rate or time saved.

argument_progression.function: Introduces a distinction between a complete-looking request and a remaining human decision.
Supplies an explicitly fictional mechanism: rule-based proposed flags, then reviewer checking before further action.
Names what the example explains and explicitly withholds two unmeasured outcomes: error rate and time saved.
Converts the distinction into a practical task: specify the reviewer decision.

evidence_reasoning_limit.evidence: An explicitly fictional workflow in paragraph 2; no real implementation or measured case is presented.
evidence_reasoning_limit.reasoning: Separating proposed flags from reviewer checking identifies a decision boundary and supports the practical instruction to name it.
evidence_reasoning_limit.limit: The example can illustrate a workflow function. It cannot establish reliable flagging, error reduction, time savings, a founder event or a customer result.

ending.function: Direct application, asking the reader to name the retained reviewer decision.
ending.engagement_or_offer: No engagement request, service promise or offer appears.

rows.visual_role: not_observable: media not supplied; text analysis does not imply the post had no media.

synthetic_counters.interpretation: Values supplied by the synthetic fixture at its stated capture time; not evidence of real-world interactions or effectiveness.

rows.bounded_lesson: Use an illustrative mechanism to make responsibility concrete, then state exactly which outcomes remain unmeasured.
rows.applicability: Adapt this function when a reader needs to assign responsibility in a proposed review workflow. Confirm any real capability separately.
gaps: No audience, impressions, reach, paid exposure, buyer fit or expressed need evidence

rows.author: Example Founder B
rows.actual_review_modality: Read the complete four-paragraph synthetic original text supplied in the test JSON; no URL access, image, video, transcript or audio review.
rows.reader_situation_and_job: A professional deciding whether to rely on an AI-generated summary needs a short review routine for its sources, quoted figures and unresolved points.

hook_and_payoff.opening_exact: Here are three checks before using an AI-generated summary.
hook_and_payoff.promise: Provide exactly three checks for reviewing a summary before use.
hook_and_payoff.delivered_payoff: Paragraph 2 supplies all three: identify the source, verify the quoted figures and retain unresolved points.
hook_and_payoff.count_check: Promised 3; delivered 3; no missing or extra check.

rows.central_claim: A polished paragraph does not itself establish that its source has been checked.

argument_progression.function: Delivers the three concrete review actions.
Explains the distinction behind the checklist: presentation quality does not substitute for source verification.
Invites the reader to identify which part they review manually.

evidence_reasoning_limit.evidence: A proposed three-action checklist and a conceptual distinction; no study, measured example or customer case is supplied.
evidence_reasoning_limit.reasoning: The three actions inspect provenance, numerical fidelity and unresolved uncertainty. These functions bear on review more directly than prose polish alone.
evidence_reasoning_limit.limit: The text does not demonstrate that the routine catches every error, produces accurate summaries or improves engagement. Any replies would be self-selected, not representative demand evidence.

ending.function: A relevant open question about the reader's current manual review, tied to the checklist.
ending.engagement_or_offer: Discussion invitation; no service offer or guaranteed outcome.

rows.visual_role: not_observable: media not supplied; no visual explanation or layout was inspected.

synthetic_counters.interpretation: Values supplied by the synthetic fixture at its stated capture time; not evidence of real-world interactions or effectiveness.

rows.bounded_lesson: Match a numbered promise to an inspectable set of actions and explain the distinction that makes those actions relevant.
rows.applicability: Adapt the checklist function when the reader needs an executable review routine. A closing question is useful only when the author actually wants that discussion.
gaps: No actual replies or audience research supplied
No impressions, reach, paid exposure, buyer relevance or conversion evidence

comparison_synthesis: Both synthetic texts deliver a bounded reader task. A explains a fictional workflow and makes its unmeasured outcomes explicit; B delivers an exact three-check promise, explains why polish is insufficient and ends with a relevant discussion question. These are observable editorial functions. The fixture gives A 31 reactions and 4 comments, and B 12 reactions and 2 comments, at matching supplied publication and capture timestamps. Those invented counts establish no real-world standout, causal mechanism or performance rule. A has no measured workflow evidence; B has no measured checklist evidence. No contrary original beyond these two records was supplied.
